questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Matters

This question tests your ability to design a complete incident response system for a critical security issue in multi-tenant infrastructure.

## Key Skills Being Tested

1. **Data Privacy Incident Response**
   - How to detect and document data leaks between tenants
   - Regulatory compliance requires evidence chain of custody

2. **Tenant Isolation Understanding**
   - Partition keys, cache isolation, query filters
   - Common failure modes (missing tenant ID, race conditions)

3. **Safe Deployment Practices**
   - Canary deployment with automatic rollback
   - Gated releases for safety-critical changes

4. **Metrics-Driven Operations**
   - Measuring detection speed and fix speed
   - Tracking recurrence to evaluate prevention effectiveness

## Simplified Structure

| Section | What It Addresses |
|---------|-------------------|
| Data Model | What to track (who, what, when, how) |
| Lifecycle | How the incident flows from detection to closure |
| API | How systems interact with CAPA data |
| Metrics | How we measure our effectiveness |
| RCA + Rollback | How to fix and prevent recurrence |

## Common Partition Bugs to Watch

- Missing tenant ID in partition key
- Cache key collision across tenants
- Race condition in partition assignment
- In-memory data not cleared between requests
- Query filter missing tenant context

The answer focuses on practical, implementable solutions rather than theoretical concepts.

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to design a CAPA (Corrective Action and Preventive Action) program for a security breach scenario in a Databricks lakehouse environment. It evaluates understanding of real components like Delta Live Tables and Unity Catalog, along with multi-tenant guardrails.

## Key Concepts

- CAPA data model with evidence, lineage, owners, and policy links
- Unity Catalog Row-Level Security (RLS)
- Delta Live Tables data lineage
- Tenant-aware lifecycle with defined SLAs
- Canary rollout and RCA templates

## Code Example

```json
POST /api/v1/capas
{
  "title": "RLS Bypass in DLT Pipeline",
  "severity": "critical",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-123",
  "evidence": {
    "timestamp": "2026-03-14T10:30:00Z",
    "user_id": "user-456",
    "query_fingerprint": "sha256:abc123...",
    "affected_tables": ["db.tbl_sensitive"]
  },
  "lineage": {
    "source": "db.tbl_sensitive",
    "pipeline": "dlt-pipeline-001",
    "target": "db.tbl_output"
  },
  "owners": {
    "data_owner": "team-data-platform@company.com",
    "security_owner": "team-security@company.com"
  },
  "policy_links": [
    "https://unitycatalog.company.com/policies/rls-v1"
  ]
}
```

## CAPA Lifecycle with Tenant-Aware SLAs

| Phase | SLA | Actions |
|-------|-----|----------|
| Detect | T+0 (15 min) | Automated alerts from Databricks audit logs |
| Contain | T+1 (4 hours) | Isolate affected pipelines, revoke transient access |
| Remediate | T+2 (72 hours) | Fix DLT query, update RLS policy |
| Verify | T+3 (7 days) | Confirm no recurrence, validate tenant isolation |

## Tenant Metrics for Containment

- Time to isolation per tenant
- Number of records exposed per tenant
- Recurrence rate within 30 days
- Policy violation frequency by pipeline
